status: current_api_behaviour: EXISTING-API conformance vectors. Every expected value is what the explicit (caller-declared) quantity-kind API of unitsml-ruby 2ec9583 returned or raised. They are not a policy decision on how kV*A should be typed.
relationship: New additive generation; no earlier file changed. The H2 raw/summary profiles (host-evaluator/v1, evaluator-reference/v1) and every existing negative boundary are untouched.
not_covered: Implicit or automatic typing of kV*A (inferring apparent power or power from the unit expression) is a future policy question and is not exercised or asserted here. No row assigns a kind the caller did not declare or the API did not return.

profiles.unitsdb-2.2.15: published unitsdb gem 2.2.15 bundled data (blobs equal to unitsdb 035665f), loaded read-only from the gem directory
profiles.unitsdb-143-b0b4315: final merged UnitsDB #143 b0b4315fc5b53f6caa0a1edb94707b4f13223b38 (tree c57eb0ae330b051e6ea7909aeabe0a89b77707ed), git archive export

loader: Unitsml::Unitsdb::Database.from_db(DATA_DIR) injected as the process's Unitsml::Unitsdb.database before any parse; ::Unitsdb.database guarded to raise in-process. The installed gem and data were not altered.

producer.runtime: ruby 4.0.1 +PRISM x86_64-linux via mise, session-local bundle, nice -n 19, TZ=UTC LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; two separate processes per profile, byte-equal

findings: Both profiles give identical results for all 22 probes; only the units.yaml digest differs between the snapshots.
Data (both profiles): NISTq187 'apparent power' and NISTq20 'power' are both NISTd16 with equivalence_class null; no unit has symbol VA or a volt-ampere name; NISTq187 is referenced only by NISTu401.

Construction: kind NISTq187 and kind NISTq20 are both accepted on kV*A (the kind gate checks dimension only); kind :primary on kV*A raises UnknownQuantityKindError; kind NISTq187 is also accepted on kW.

convert_to('kW') preserves the caller-declared kind (NISTq187 stays NISTq187, value 3/1); it is not refused, although the target kW has primary kind NISTq20. An untyped kV*A converts to an untyped kW.
Typed NISTq187 with NISTq20 (+ and -, same unit or kV*A with kW) raises QuantityKindMismatchError 'no shared equivalence class'; == returns false. NISTq187 + NISTq187 is legal.
An untyped operand keeps dimension-only gating and the result takes the typed operand's kind (kV*A untyped + kW NISTq20 gives kind NISTq20, in kV*A).
The untyped product kV * A, and parsed kV*A, have kind nil and primary_kind nil (composite expression, no single unit record). This is actual source behaviour, not an inferred power kind.
remaining_policy_question: Owner (UnitsDB/UnitsML): should kV*A be typed implicitly (e.g. a VA unit with primary NISTq187, or a shared equivalence class), and should convert_to refuse a typed source whose kind differs from the target unit's primary kind? Neither is current API behaviour; the vectors here pin the current explicit-kind behaviour only.
